$comment: Intended Firebase layout for nextjs-revalidator. Auth = Firebase Authentication (email/password); site data = Firestore, scoped per user by Auth UID. Secrets live only in Firestore and are never sent to the browser (except on-demand for preview-channel sites).

auth.notes: Users are created in the Firebase console (Authentication tab). There is no in-app self-registration. Passwords are verified server-side via the Identity Toolkit REST API using FIREBASE_API_KEY.

company.title: Company
company.description: A brand grouping site environments, owned by a single user.

sites.description: SiteEntry objects. Each includes the server-only `secret` plus url, environment, channel, and optional last* revalidation status fields.

secret.description: Bearer token. NEVER returned to the browser via the site list.

/users/{userId}/companies/{companyId}.description: Per-user company site groups. {userId} is the Firebase Auth UID. Written only by the server (Admin SDK).

security.rules: Because all reads/writes go through the server using the Admin SDK (which bypasses security rules), lock client access down. Recommended rules deny all client access: `match /{document=**} { allow read, write: if false; }`. The app never uses the Firebase client SDK for Firestore.
